title: Introduce semantic failure attributor and soft-fail sentinel
author: Sophie Martinez
description: Motivation: Flaky prompt-set failures often surface as noisy, undiagnosed regressions. This PR adds a semantic failure attributor that groups failing outputs by semantic equivalence (embedding + cluster heuristics) and attaches a compact explanation blob. In parallel it introduces a soft-fail sentinel CI hook that will let teams mark transient regressions as soft failures for a configurable backoff window while still surfacing them in dashboards. The goal is to reduce alert fatigue and give engineers richer failure context to triage root causes quickly. Changes include: new attributor service, CLI matcher for historic failure lookups, CI hook that can soft-fail with TTL/backoff, telemetry events, and dashboard links. Checklist: 1) Implement semantic clustering with cosine threshold + token-match heuristics; 2) Add exporter for compact failure blobs and anchor examples; 3) Integrate soft-fail sentinel into existing CI pipeline with opt-in label support; 4) Add unit tests and end-to-end smoke job; 5) Update docs and rollout playbook. Related work: this complements ENG-3980 (prompt-set bank) and follows patterns from recent drift-detection services. Linear: ENG-4123. Jira: SUP-786 for customer incident that motivated the emergency hold behavior.
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial semantic attributor implementation; add CI soft-fail hook and TTL policy; add telemetry and dashboard link attachments; tests and docs. Commits include focused refactors to the eval runner to expose failure hooks and a small shim to serialize failure blobs for downstream debugging.
diff_snippets:
+ def compute_semantic_signature(text):
+     	sig = embed(text)[:128]  # truncated vector for grouping
+     return sha1(sig.tobytes()).hexdigest()

+ class SoftFailSentinel(Hook):
+     	def on_eval_complete(self, result):
+     		if is_transient(result):
+     			mark_soft_fail(result, ttl_seconds=86400)  # default 1 day
- removed obsolete flaky_gate flag from eval runner configuration

ci_notes: integration-smoke initially failed due to external embed service timeout; retried and passed. e2e-canine run included canary tag and used local mock embedder for stability.
testing_notes: Local unit tests added for clustering logic, sampling logic validated with synthetic failure corpus. Ran a staged canary on 'eval-team' with 48h observation window; soft-fail rate reduced alert noise by ~38% on sampled prompts.
release_notes: Add semantic failure attribution and configurable soft-fail sentinel to CI. Enables grouping of semantically equivalent failures and optional soft-fail behavior to reduce noisy regression alerts. Backwards compatible; opt-in via feature flag.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: enable in eval-team canary (2 days). Stage 2: enable for platform team and monitor failure export volume (1 week). Stage 3: org-wide enablement with default soft-fail TTL 24h and sampling rate 0.1. Rollback: flip feature flag off and purge soft-fail queue.
post_merge_actions: Add feature flag to infra for org rollout
Schedule dashboard panels to show soft-fail vs hard-fail rates
Follow-up PR to add retention policy for exported failure blobs
notes_on_backward_compatibility: All changes are opt-in; existing eval runners default to previous behavior unless feature flag enabled. Failure blobs are stored under a new keyspace and will not affect current alerting unless teams opt-in to the sentinel.
security_considerations: Failure blobs may contain PII or user content. Exporter defaults to scrub mode: remove email addresses, phone numbers, and long personal identifiers. Teams must opt-in via an enterprise policy for full payload exports and enable KMS encryption. KMS tag: redwood-eval-failure-exports.
maintainer_notes: Keep an eye on daily exported blob count; sampling defaults can be tuned per-organization. The clustering threshold is conservative by default (cosine >= 0.86). If the embedding provider changes, re-run baseline to recalibrate thresholds.
human_summary: This merged change reduces noisy CI alerts by grouping semantically similar failures and letting teams mark certain regressions as soft failures for a configurable window while providing richer context to triage. Authored by Sophie Martinez and approved after canary testing.
